issues.legal_issue: Bare non-service of summons, without more, does not constitute fraud sufficient to maintain an independent suit to set aside a decree.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought an independent suit to set aside an ex parte decree, alleging that it had been obtained by fraud and misrepresentation because summons had not been served and the defendant had not given a proper name and address.
The plaintiff had earlier sought to set aside the decree for non-service and appealed against it, but did not allege fraud in either proceeding.
The court found no evidence of fraud beyond the allegation of non-service.
issues.conclusion: An independent suit to set aside a decree on the alleged ground of fraud is not maintainable where the only fraud alleged is bare non-service of summons; non-service alone did not establish fraud in this case.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the suit was framed as an independent civil action to set aside the decree. The court relied on Choksi Bhidarbhai Mathurbhai v. Purshottamdas Bhogilal Shah, AIR 1962 Gujarat 10, for the principle that a suit to set aside a decree on fraud is not maintainable where the only fraud alleged is bare non-service of summons.

predicates.independent_decree_fraud_suit: A claimant brings an independent suit seeking to set aside a decree on the ground that it was obtained by fraud.
predicates.summons_nonservice_only: The claimant alleges no fraud beyond the fact that summons was not served.

issues.definition: When a claimant brings an independent suit to set aside a decree for fraud and alleges only non-service of summons, the suit is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: Fraud in obtaining a decree must be specifically pleaded and established by strong proof that a representation was knowingly false or made without reasonable belief in its truth.
material_facts: The independent suit alleged fraud in connection with the name and address given for the defendant and the service of summons.
The plaintiff had not alleged fraud in the earlier application to set aside the ex parte decree or in the appeal from it.

The court found only a bare allegation of fraud and no evidence that a representation was false to the knowledge of the person making it or that the person could have had no reasonable belief that it was true.
issues.conclusion: Fraud was not established, and the appeal was dismissed. A bare or ambiguous allegation does not satisfy the demanding proof required to establish fraud.
issues.legal_principle: Fraud must be pleaded and proved. The representation must be shown to have been false to the knowledge of the person making it, or to have been made when that person could have had no reasonable belief that it was true; the required level of proof is extremely high, and an ambiguous statement does not by itself establish fraud. The court relied on Pollock & Mulla on Indian Contract & Specific Relief Acts, 12th edition (2001), page 489.

predicates.independent_decree_fraud_suit: A claimant brings an independent suit seeking to set aside a decree on the ground that it was obtained by fraud.
predicates.fraud_not_proved_to_heightened_standard: The claimant does not establish by strong proof that a representation was knowingly false or made without reasonable belief in its truth.

issues.definition: In an independent suit to set aside a decree for fraud, failure to establish fraud by the required strong proof means that the fraud claim fails.
